A hardware-accelerated QML item that draws a grid of values as colored cells.

detaileddescription.para: The grid has columns cells per row and rows rows of cells. Values are stored row by row: the value of a cell has index row * columns + column, with row 0 at yMin and column 0 at xMin. xMin, xMax, yMin, and yMax are the outer edges of the grid; an unset bound places the grid in index space, so column c spans [c, c + 1].

Each cell is colored by mapping its value through colormap. The series starts with a Viridis colormap of its own whose range is resolved from the data; assign a shared Colormap to replace it. Nothing is drawn while colormap is null. The series has no legend entry: a ColorBar is its key.

simplesect.title: Data
simplesect.para: setValues() replaces the values and the shape together. The PlotSeries setters take one value per cell and keep columns, so their count must be a multiple of it. DataBounds passed to them replace the grid edges as the data range until the values, the shape, or an edge next changes. Values are stored in single precision. postValues() and postData() may be called from any thread.

simplesect.title: Invalid cells
simplesect.para: Cells with a non-finite value, and cells with a value at or below zero under a Log colormap, are transparent. Non-finite values do not count toward the value range.

simplesect.title: Logarithmic axes and spacing
simplesect.para: xSpacing and ySpacing space the cells evenly in data or in log10, independently of the axis scale. On a log axis, Log cells have equal widths, Linear cells narrow toward larger values, and the parts of cells at or below zero are not drawn; the data range starts at the first cell edge above zero. Under Log spacing, both edges of that dimension must be positive, so set them: an unset edge resolves to index space, which starts at 0. Otherwise the series draws nothing, reports no data range in that dimension, and logs a warning.

simplesect.title: Inspection
simplesect.para: inspection.recordAt() and inspection.recordAtPosition() return a record with the fields x and y (the cell center, geometric under Log spacing), value, row, and column. inspection.dataPointAtPosition() returns the cell as a data point at its center, with index row * columns + column, which PlotInspector reports in every mode. A cell with a non-finite value is still a match. While a grid edge is not finite, or not positive under Log spacing, recordAt() returns Unavailable and no position matches a cell.

simplesect.title: Limits
simplesect.para: Each pixel takes the color of the cell under its center, without interpolation. A grid with an infinite edge draws nothing. A grid of more than 16,777,216 (2^24) columns or rows, or of more cells than the GPU data texture holds, about 67 million for an 8192-pixel texture limit, draws nothing and logs a warning.
